Maintenance Report — MNT-0138-007

Asset: WELL-0138 (NE-07 Well 138, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 28 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Nov 2023 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 235 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0138-0054 on 2023-10-26 Report written: 08 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0138-0054 showed the wellhead at 27.2 °C with the air at 18.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0138-0080 showed the wellhead at 31.5 °C with the air at 23.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 14 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0138-0195 showed the wellhead at 38.3 °C with the air at 34.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

maintenance.action: Replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0138-034

Asset: WELL-0138 (NE-07 Well 138, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 02 Oct 2026 08:00 · Finished: 12 Oct 2026 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 252 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0138-0206 on 2026-10-01 Report written: 13 Oct 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0138-0206 showed the wellhead at 29.8 °C with the air at 24.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste
